headline: Low prompt-injection and data-leakage risk; no direct shared-channel or write-conflict evidence between Great Expectations and LangChain4j.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Great Expectations can read and emit validation results and documentation, while LangChain4j is a customer-support orchestration library. No shared channel is documented, so prompt injection is not evidenced; however, if Great Expectations outputs are manually copied into LangChain4j prompts, the bridge could be abused. Uncertainty keeps this above none.
conditions: IF Great Expectations outputs are manually pasted into LangChain4j prompts, attacker-controlled text can influence downstream instructions.
IF an external workflow bridges validation results into chat prompts without sanitization, injection becomes plausible.
mitigations: Use a fixed template that strips instructions from validation text.
Paste only summarized metrics, not raw reports.
Add a review step before any LangChain4j prompt uses Great Expectations output.
requires-engineering: implement provenance tagging between tools.
requires-engineering: add prompt-content allowlisting.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Great Expectations touches data sources, validation results, and documentation, but its network egress is none. LangChain4j also shows no egress and no data classes touched. With no shared workspace or upload path documented, leakage is not evidenced; the remaining risk is limited to local exposure if operators co-locate sensitive files.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same local workspace, validation artifacts may be visible across tools.
IF operators place sensitive data in shared files, local disclosure becomes possible.
mitigations: Keep each agent in a separate directory.
Store sensitive inputs in access-controlled folders.
Delete temporary validation artifacts after use.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent filesystem isolation.
requires-engineering: add DLP scanning on shared outputs.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Great Expectations has package installation and file I/O surfaces, but LangChain4j exposes no write surfaces, OAuth scopes, or concurrency model here. Without overlapping mutable resources, a write conflict pathway is not supported by the profiles. The interaction is therefore provably absent from the documented surfaces.
conditions: IF LangChain4j is extended with filesystem or database writes to the same target as Great Expectations, conflict risk would emerge.
IF both agents are later granted shared mutable OAuth scopes, contention becomes possible.
mitigations: Keep LangChain4j read-only in this workflow.
Avoid sharing writable directories.
Run one agent at a time for any future shared resource.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared state.
requires-engineering: define explicit ownership for mutable resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Great Expectations produces validation results that LangChain4j could render or act on in a support workflow. Because LangChain4j is a general orchestration layer and no verification step is documented, A's output may become B's input by default in downstream automation. The blast radius is multiple work products, though not directly irreversible from the profiles alone.
conditions: IF LangChain4j consumes Great Expectations validation results as authoritative text, downstream actions may propagate errors.
IF support responses are generated from unverified validation output, incorrect conclusions can cascade.
mitigations: Require human review before sending any response.
Add a verification checklist for validation claims.
Pass only structured fields, not free text.
requires-engineering: add schema validation between agents.
requires-engineering: separate generation from action-taking.

E_compliance.rationale: Great Expectations touches data quality tests, validation results, and documentation, while LangChain4j shows no data classes touched and no residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented. With no compliance-sensitive data flow evidenced, a compliance breach pathway is not supported by the profiles.
conditions: IF future deployments route regulated data through LangChain4j, compliance review would be needed.
IF retention or residency policies are added later, the pair should be re-evaluated.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of this pair.
Document data-handling boundaries.
Review retention settings before deployment.
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for regulated datasets.
requires-engineering: map residency and retention controls explicitly.
